title: Minimal prep veneers vs no-prep veneers: what 0.3 mm really means
seoTitle: Minimal Prep vs No-Prep Veneers: The 0.3 mm Truth
description: No-prep, prepless and minimal prep veneers compared: enamel removed, who is a candidate, why no-prep can look bulky, and what each one costs.
author: Dr. Marta Puentes Marrero, DMD
imageAlt: A wafer-thin porcelain veneer held up to the window light between gloved fingertips, the light glowing through it
answer: **No-prep veneers** are bonded over untouched enamel; **minimal prep veneers** remove **about 0.3 mm**, roughly the thickness of a contact lens, so the veneer sits flush instead of adding bulk. Both keep the bond on enamel: no nerve, no crown. No-prep suits small or set-back teeth; minimal prep suits almost everyone else. At Xiluet Smiles every veneer is 0.3 mm, and preparation is decided tooth by tooth.

sections.h2: Three words for the same idea, and one real difference

blocks.p: Search for veneers and you meet three terms. **No-prep veneers** (also sold as prepless veneers or under brand names such as Lumineers) are bonded directly to the tooth with no enamel removed. **Minimal prep veneers** remove a very thin layer, typically 0.3 to 0.5 mm, where the veneer will sit. **Conventional veneers** remove 0.5 to 0.7 mm or more. Everything else about the three, the porcelain, the bonding, the lab work, is the same.

The real difference is not reversibility, which is the word the no-prep marketing leans on. It is whether the veneer adds thickness to the tooth or replaces thickness that was removed. Add 0.3 mm to a tooth that is already in the right place and the tooth gets 0.3 mm bigger: a little fuller at the gum line, a little more forward, a little harder to clean at the margin. Replace 0.3 mm and the tooth stays the size it was, with a new surface.

blocks.p: A sheet of printer paper is 0.1 mm. A soft contact lens is a little under 0.1 mm at the center and thicker at the edge. Front-tooth enamel is about 1 mm thick. So 0.3 mm is three sheets of paper, or a thick contact lens, taken from a layer that is three times deeper. The nerve is a further 2 to 3 mm behind that, inside the dentin. Nothing in a 0.3 mm preparation comes near it.

That is why the question "do veneers ruin your teeth" has two answers. Aggressive preparations that cut into dentin to make room for thick veneers, the ones behind the ["Turkey teeth" photos](/blog/do-veneers-ruin-your-teeth), can. A 0.3 mm preparation in enamel does not. The tooth under a minimal prep veneer looks like the tooth you had, very slightly matte where it was smoothed. [What teeth look like under veneers](/blog/what-do-teeth-look-like-under-veneers) has photos.

blocks.quote: Patients ask for no-prep because they are afraid of the drill. What they actually want is to keep their enamel and keep the option of a different dentist in 15 years. 0.3 mm gives them both, without the bulk.

sections.h2: When no-prep veneers are the right call

blocks.p: No-prep is not a gimmick. On the right tooth it is the best option, because adding a thin shell is exactly what the tooth needs. The pattern is teeth that are already smaller than the smile wants them to be.

list: **Small or peg-shaped lateral incisors.** The two teeth either side of the front pair are often narrow; a no-prep veneer builds them out to match.
**Gaps.** Closing a 1 to 2 mm gap means making two teeth slightly wider. No enamel needs to come off to do that.
**Set-back teeth.** A tooth that sits behind its neighbors gains the thickness of the veneer and comes into line.
**Worn, shortened edges.** Veneers that extend the edge add length without touching the face of the tooth.
**After braces or Invisalign,** when the alignment is right and only shape and color need finishing.

blocks.p: In these cases our 0.3 mm veneers are placed with little or no preparation, which is why the [porcelain veneers page](/porcelain-veneers-miami) says "0.3 mm, sometimes none". The decision is made tooth by tooth at the design visit, from the scan and the mock-up, not as a package you choose in advance.

sections.h2: When no-prep goes wrong: bulk, margins and the gum line

blocks.p: Put a no-prep veneer on a tooth that is already the right size and in the right position, and three things happen. The tooth gets thicker, so the smile reads as fuller and sometimes "toothy". The edge of the veneer at the gum line has to stop somewhere, and with no preparation there is no ledge for it to finish in, so it sits proud of the tooth, which traps plaque and can inflame the gum. And on anything but a light tooth, 0.3 mm of untouched porcelain over a dark base shows the base through.

None of this is a flaw in the ceramic. It is geometry. The [ADA's patient guidance](https://www.mouthhealthy.org/all-topics-a-z/veneers) is careful to say that no-prep veneers suit some patients, not all, and that is the honest position. The clinics to be wary of are the ones that sell no-prep as the answer for every mouth, because the mouths it does not suit end up with the bulky, opaque result people associate with bad veneers. [Why some veneers look fake](/blog/why-veneers-look-fake) goes through the signs.

sections.h2: What minimal prep changes, tooth by tooth

blocks.p: Minimal preparation is not a fixed 0.3 mm shaved off every tooth. It is a design-led decision. Because the final shape of each tooth is already approved as a mock-up before the preparation visit, the doctor knows where the veneer needs room and where it does not. A tooth that leans forward is reduced a little more on its front face; a set-back tooth is barely touched; a stained tooth gets just enough reduction for the ceramist to layer an opaque base under the translucent edge.

steps: **Mock-up first.** The approved design is placed over your teeth in resin. Where the mock-up is thin or absent, nothing needs preparing.
**Reduction through the mock-up.** Tiny depth grooves are cut through the resin, not the tooth, so the preparation is measured against the final shape rather than guessed.
**Enamel only.** The area is numbed for comfort, but the work stays in the outer third of the enamel. If a tooth would need more, the plan says crown, and the estimate said so before you booked.
**Margin at the gum line.** A fine finish line lets the veneer end flush with the tooth, where you can floss it, rather than under the gum where margins are hidden and gums suffer.

blocks.p: The material matters here too. Our veneers are milled from multilayer zirconia at about 0.3 mm, which is strong enough at that thickness to cover a darker tooth without being made thicker. Older feldspathic porcelains needed 0.5 mm or more to do the same job, which is where the conventional preparation numbers come from. The [zirconia versus e.max](/blog/zirconia-veneers-vs-emax-veneers) comparison covers the strength figures.

sections.h2: Cost: no-prep veneers vs minimal prep veneers

blocks.p: No-prep veneers are not cheaper. Branded no-prep systems are usually priced at or above conventional veneers, because the brand licenses the name and the lab work is the same. Published US ranges put a single porcelain veneer at $925 to $2,500, with branded no-prep at the upper half of that. Thickness changes the technique, not the ceramist's hours.

sections.h2: How to choose, in three questions

list: **Are my teeth small, gappy or set back?** Then no preparation may be right, and a clinic that does 0.3 mm veneers can place them that way. You do not need a branded system to get a no-prep result.
**Are my teeth normal-sized, stained or slightly crowded?** Then minimal preparation of about 0.3 mm will look better and clean better than adding a shell on top.
**Is anyone proposing 0.7 mm or more, or a crown, for a healthy front tooth?** Ask why. Sometimes there is a reason, such as an old large filling. Often there is not.

blocks.p: If you want the decision made from your own teeth rather than a label, send three photos through the [free photo evaluation](/free-photo-evaluation). The plan you get back says, for each tooth, veneer or crown, and the mock-up at Visit 1 shows where preparation is needed and where it is not. The whole process is described in [the veneers procedure, step by step](/blog/porcelain-veneers-procedure-step-by-step).

faq.a: Partly. The enamel underneath is untouched, so in theory a no-prep veneer can be removed and the tooth is as it was. In practice removal takes a dentist, a drill and care not to scratch the enamel, and the bonding resin has to be polished off. It is better to think of both no-prep and 0.3 mm veneers as enamel-preserving rather than reversible.

faq.q: How thick is a minimal prep veneer?
faq.a: About 0.3 mm at Xiluet Smiles, roughly the thickness of a contact lens or three sheets of paper. Front-tooth enamel is about 1 mm thick, so the preparation stays in its outer third and the nerve, 2 to 3 mm further in, is never approached.

On teeth that are already the right size, often yes: the veneer adds its full thickness to the tooth and the margin at the gum line has nowhere to finish. On small, short or set-back teeth, no, because the added thickness is exactly what the design calls for. The tooth decides, not the product.

faq.q: Can no-prep veneers cover dark or stained teeth?
faq.a: Poorly. With no room made, the veneer has to be thin and translucent, and a dark tooth shows through. Minimal preparation of about 0.3 mm gives the ceramist room to layer an opaque base under a translucent edge, which is how a stained tooth ends up looking natural rather than grey or chalky.

faq.q: Are minimal prep veneers more expensive than no-prep?
faq.a: No. At Xiluet Smiles a veneer is $1,000 whether or not the tooth is prepared, and 20 veneers are $5,999 as the Smile Design package. Branded no-prep systems elsewhere are usually priced at or above conventional veneers because the lab work is the same and the name is licensed.

faq.q: Do minimal prep veneers need anesthetic?
faq.a: We numb the area for comfort, because three hours in the chair is easier that way, but the preparation itself stays in enamel, which has no nerve endings. Patients with no-prep teeth in the same set simply have those teeth cleaned and bonded. Sensitivity afterwards, if any, lasts a day or two.
